title: Expressions and operator order
goals: Evaluate numeric expressions using Python’s grouping rules
Use parentheses to express the intended calculation
Distinguish ordinary division, whole groups and a remainder
vocabulary: Code evaluated to produce a value
A symbol such as + or * that specifies an operation
Rules that determine how an expression is grouped
Symbols that make a grouping explicit
The amount left after forming whole groups

blocks.text: The first line groups subtraction from left to right: (20 - 6) - 2 gives 12. The second gives 16. Multiplication and division share a precedence level, so 12 / 3 * 2 groups as (12 / 3) * 2 and displays 8.0, not 2.0. Ordinary / division produces a float, even when the result is mathematically whole.

blocks.label: Explain why 18 - 4 * 3 gives 6 while (18 - 4) * 3 gives 42. Which operation is grouped first in each expression?

guided_practice.title: Predict then test expressions
guided_practice.prompt: Predict 16 - 5 - 3, 16 - (5 - 3), and 18 / 3 * 2. Write the grouping, run each line and record actual results separately.
guided_practice.answer: (16 - 5) - 3 is 8; 16 - (5 - 3) is 14; (18 / 3) * 2 is 12.0. Record any observed discrepancy and check the saved expression rather than copying expected results.

blocks.title: Two expressions with different meanings
blocks.caption: Adding two inside every pack differs from adding two loose counters once.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
packs = 3
per_pack = 8
loose = 2
total = packs * per_pack + loose
print(total)

The script displays 26. Replacing the total expression with packs * (per_pack + loose) displays 30, because it adds two to every pack. Parentheses are not decoration: they can change the represented situation. Write a brief phrase for each group before running.
